title: ISTANBUL TURKEY 2025 | Sirkeci & Eminonu Daily Life - Street Food Paradise - 4K Walking Tour
description:
Explore Sirkeci & Eminonu—Galata Bridge views, Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar), ferries, and iconic street food like balık ekmek, simit, and midye. A real daily-life (4K Walking Tour) through Istanbul’s most vibrant waterfront. (Eminönü/Eminonu)
Walk the historic waterfront of Istanbul through Sirkeci & Eminönü—a street-food paradise with Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar) aromas, Galata Bridge views, and real daily life in 4K.
See ferries on the Bosphorus, the T1 Tram, and iconic bites: balık ekmek, simit, midye dolma, döner, kokoreç, and fresh pomegranate juice
Explore Eminönü (Eminonu)—the beating heart of Istanbul’s Old City—where Galata Bridge links to Karaköy and fishermen line the rails all day. From the Bosphorus and Golden Horn you’ll watch city ferries glide to Kadıköy and Üsküdar, with postcard views of Galata Tower. Around Eminönü Square, the T1 Tram rattles past the Yeni Camii (New Mosque) and the waterfront market stalls selling fish sandwiches (balık ekmek), roasted chestnuts, and simit.

Dive into the legendary Spice Bazaar / Egyptian Bazaar for Istanbul’s most colorful flavors: saffron, sumac, Turkish delight, nuts, dried fruits, baklava, and lokum. Hidden nearby, the Rüstem Paşa Mosque shines with İznik tiles, while lanes around Tahtakale buzz with tea shops, copperware, and spice merchants. This is real Istanbul daily life—vendors calling out prices, locals commuting, and travelers tasting their way through the bazaar.

Cross into Sirkeci, the historic rail gateway of the Orient Express at Sirkeci Station. Wander narrow backstreets packed with döner, kokoreç, köfte, pide, and family-run lokantas. Landmarks include the Grand Post Office (Büyük Postane) and Hoca Paşa cultural venues, while the Sirkeci ferry piers connect the European and Asian sides in minutes. Cafés, bakeries, and Hafız Mustafa-style dessert shops keep the sugar energy high for a full walking tour.
Practical vibes: This route is perfect for sunset (golden hour) when Galata Bridge glows and the Bosphorus turns mirror-blue. It’s easy to access via T1 (Eminönü/Sirkeci) and by city ferries. Expect crowds, street performers, and bargain shopping for gifts and spices. title: Hiking Eagle Creek, From First to Last Waterfall - No Talk, No Music, Just Nature. - 4K Virtual Hike
description:
A virtual walk & hike on Oregon's Eagle Creek Trail to Tunnel Falls, with no talk, no music, no close-up shots of my ugly mug... just nature & relaxation. The full journey in real-time, 4K video.

In the heart of the Columbia River Gorge - a swath of the lush Cascade Range cut in two by Ice Age floods (and a fave weekend getaway for Portlanders) - crystal-clear Eagle Creek rushes down the rainforest-like slopes, carving its own stunning gorge along the way. (A gorge within a gorge, if you will. Gorge-ception!). Truly one of the iconic walks of the PNW.

An astoundingly-built trail traces the creek's many twists, turns, and drops, often on cliffs high above where the path is blasted straight from rock, with narrow tread, steep drops, and a chain handhold to keep you steady. It's all worth it, because the hike also features stately forest, wildflowers, countless waterfalls, and lots and lots of water.

Eagle Creek is also famous as ground zero for an infamous wildfire in 2017 - the area is still recovering, which means many acres of burned trees but also slightly improved views all around.

Our outing goes far beyond where most hikers turn around, past impressive Punchbowl Falls (unfortunately high water prevents a side-trip down for a closer look, but the viewpoint from above is great), High Bridge, roaring Tunnel Falls (which yes, does feature a tunnel), distinctive Twister Falls, before ending at little-visited Sevenmile Falls - the last major cascade on the trail. Enjoy!

description:
Experience the magic of Tokyo's Ginza Luxury Shopping District like never before with our immersive 4K walking tour! Dive into the world of luxury with our exclusive 4K walking tour of Tokyo's most prestigious districts!

In the first part of our journey, we explore the opulent streets of Ginza Luxury Shopping District, home to renowned brands like Chanel, Prada, Hermes, Louis Vuitton, and Tiffany's.

Stroll along the elegant Chuo-dori street as raindrops delicately fall, casting a serene ambiance over the glitzy storefronts and modern architecture. Indulge your senses as we showcase the epitome of luxury and sophistication in this iconic neighbourhood.

But our adventure doesn't end there! Join us as we transition to the vibrant energy of Shinjuku, where luxury meets street fashion in a captivating fusion. Wander through the bustling streets adorned with prestigious boutiques like Hermes and Coach, then immerse yourself in the eclectic world of Harajuku's shopping district.

From high-end brands to quirky street fashion, experience the dynamic contrast that defines Tokyo's diverse fashion landscape.

The Bosporus Strait is a natural strait and an internationally significant waterway located in Istanbul in northwestern Turkey that connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara. It forms part of the continental boundary between Asia and Europe, and divides Turkey by separating Anatolia from Thrace. It is the world's narrowest strait used for international navigation.

Most of the shores of the Bosporus Strait, except for the area to the north, are heavily settled, with the city of Istanbul's metropolitan population of 17 million inhabitants extending inland from both banks.

The Bosporus Strait and the Dardanelles Strait at the opposite end of the Sea of Marmara are together known as the Turkish Straits.

Sections of the shore of the Bosporus in Istanbul have been reinforced with concrete or rubble and those sections of the Strait prone to deposition are periodically dredged.

title: Istanbul Turkey Walking Tour 4K | kadıköy Istanbul City 2021 | 4K 60fps (UHD) | my delicious trips
description:
Istanbul Turkey Walking Tour 4K | kadıköy Istanbul City 2021 | 4K 60fps (UHD) | my delicious trips
Kadikoy, with its lively atmosphere and city life, historical buildings, being an important transportation hub, market, large young and student population, cultural events & arts, shopping centers, cafes, pubs and restaurants by the seaside and inland and lively nightlife especially along its famous “Bar Street” and the nearby residential suburb of beautiful Moda, is one of the most popular and colorful districts of Istanbul. In Kadikoy you may experience and enjoy how the Istanbul locals live.
Kadikoy in Turkish means “the Village of the Judge”. Kadikoy was once a separate settlement area while standing the Byzantium across the Bosphorus on the historical peninsula. History of the Kadikoy dates back to the Chalcedon of the Megarians, 635 BC.
Strolling around the Kadikoy Sqaure, Moda and Fenerbahce Kalamis area and watching the crowd, having a rest and drinking tea or coffee at the various cafes nearby the sea, visiting Bahariye Street and make shopping are the best things to do in Kadikoy. The Kadikoy shoreline is very popular with the young people
Kadikoy Market and the famous Bahariye Street are the most popular places to visit and see in Kadikoy. The Kadikoy market area is also known as “the Beyoglu of the Istanbul’s Asian side”, and Bahariye street as “the Istiklal Street of Istanbul’s Asian side”. There are wide range of places at the Kadikoy market area from greengrocers to fishmongers, from spice shops to patisseries, cafes, pubs and restaurants.

The famous fish market in the Market area is worth a visit and see. The Tellalzade Street along the Kadikoy market area is famous for its antique shops and second-hand bookstores. Before you get to the Bahariye Street, on the way you’ll come across to the other famous Sanatcilar (Artists) Street and here you may find variety of pretty ceramics, paintings and art shops by the local ceramics artists.
The traffic free Bahariye Street can be considered as the most lively and famous place in Kadikoy. There is also an old fashioned tram operating from Kadikoy harbor. Bahariye Street is always lively and crowded. You may find variety of lovely cafes, pubs, bars and restaurants as well as quality shops and cultural event centers in the Bahariye Street. The Sureyya Opera House is the most eye catching building in the Bahariye Street.

Hey there! This 4K Istanbul walking tour takes you through Şile, a charming famous coastal town on the Asian side of Istanbul, known for its historic lighthouse, cozy town center, and breathtaking views of the Black Sea. Filmed in real time with no music and no commentary in sunny day of May 2026, this immersive city walk captures busy streets, local markets, cafés, waterfront views, and the energetic daily life that defines Şile.

title: Venice, Italy Ultimate Walking Tour – Rialto, San Marco & Historic Venice | 4K 60fps
description:
Venice Ultimate walking tour — Part 1 of a 7-hour walk through the historic center of Venice, Italy, starting at the Rialto Bridge and covering the Fish Market, Piazza San Marco, the Bridge of Sighs, Campo Santi Giovanni e Paolo, and countless hidden campos and canals off the tourist path. Filmed in 4K60fps with binaural audio.

Venice was built on 118 small islands in a saltwater lagoon and has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1987. This walk begins near the Rialto Bridge — completed in 1591 by Antonio da Ponte — and spends nearly 4 hours through the labyrinthine alleys, hidden campos, and working neighborhoods of San Marco, Castello, and Cannaregio.

Ideal for virtual travel, treadmill walks, and ambient atmosphere. Best with headphones.

⭐ Don't miss: Rialto Bridge at 4:38, the Fish Market at 33:35, the Scenic Rooftop Terrace at 58:26, Piazza San Marco at 1:31:55, St. Mark's Campanile view at 1:41:17, the Bridge of Sighs at 2:03:52, the Amazing Book Store (Libreria Acqua Alta) at 2:47:26, and the grocery store inside an old theater at 3:49:12.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Venice was the capital of the Republic of Venice, one of the most powerful maritime states in Europe, from the late 7th century until Napoleon's conquest in 1797. The city was built on 118 small islands connected by more than 400 bridges across 177 canals, and has remained substantially unchanged since the 18th century. This walk spends time in the sestieri of San Marco, Castello, and Cannaregio — home of the Jewish Ghetto, the first in Europe, established in 1516. The Libreria Acqua Alta, visited at 2:47:26, is one of the most unusual bookstores in the world: books are stored in gondolas and bathtubs to protect them from the acqua alta floods.

title: Rome Italy 🇮🇹 Beautiful sunny day discovering the Eternal City | Bustling City Streets Walk [4K]
description:
SUBSCRIBE for more videos: https://www.youtube.com/c/KrielJan?sub_confirmation=1
SUPPORT Kriel Jan via PayPal 🙏: https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=JMWFKQFYXXTTJ

Rome is Italy’s capital and its most populous municipality. It also serves as the administrative center of the Lazio region and the Metropolitan City of Rome. Often called the “City of Seven Hills” because of its landscape, it is also known as the “Eternal City.” Widely regarded as a cornerstone of Western civilization and Christian culture, Rome is the heart of the Catholic Church.

With a history stretching back over 28 centuries, Rome’s origins are steeped in legend, with mythology placing its founding around 753 BC—though the area had been inhabited long before then. This makes it one of the oldest continuously occupied cities in Europe. Its early inhabitants included Latins, Etruscans, and Sabines, and over time it rose to become the capital of the Roman Kingdom, the Roman Republic, and eventually the Roman Empire. Many consider it the world’s first true imperial city and metropolis. The term “Eternal City” was first used by the poet Tibullus in the 1st century BC and later echoed by writers like Ovid, Virgil, and Livy. Rome is also known as Caput Mundi, meaning “Capital of the World.”

In 2019, Rome ranked as the 14th most visited city globally, attracting 8.6 million tourists. It was the third most visited city in the European Union and Italy’s top travel destination. Its historic center is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Today, Rome remains one of the world’s leading tourist destinations, celebrated for its vast array of archaeological and artistic treasures. Visitors are drawn not only to its historic landmarks but also to its rich traditions, scenic views, and the grandeur of its famous villas and parks. Highlights include its renowned museums—such as the Capitoline Museums, the Vatican Museums, and the Galleria Borghese—alongside aqueducts, fountains, churches, palaces, ancient ruins like the Roman Forum, and the Catacombs.

title: Chicago O'Hare - Entire Airport Walking Tour
description:
Please enjoy this 4K walking tour of Terminal 1, Terminal 2, and Terminal 3 of Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD).

In this video, I start at the C Gates in Terminal 1. I take the underground tunnel to the B Gates, which are also in Terminal 1. Terminal 1 gates are mostly used for United Airlines.

I then make my way to Terminal 2 and walk around the E Gates and the F Gates. Airlines such as Air Canada, Air France, and Aeromexico operate out of Terminal 2.

Finally, I cover all of the Terminal 3 gates, which include the G Gates, the H Gates, the K Gates, and the L Gates. The Terminal 3 gates are mostly used for American Airlines.

I did not make it to Terminal 5, the international terminal. You can go to the international terminal without leaving security, but you have to take a bus. I was afraid that they were going to make me show a boarding pass for a flight leaving from Terminal 5 in order to get on the bus, so I didn't bother trying.

At around 25:50 an annoying guy is talking super loud on the phone about how he knows how to illegally collect unemployment in any state.

From Wikipedia:
"George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IATA: IAH, ICAO: KIAH, FAA LID: IAH) is the main international airport in Houston, Texas, United States, serving the Greater Houston metropolitan area. Initially named Houston Intercontinental Airport upon its opening in 1969, it was renamed in honor of George H. W. Bush, the 41st president of the United States and a resident of Houston, in 1997. It is also commonly called Houston International Airport or George Bush International Airport.

Located about 23 miles (37 km) north of Downtown Houston between Interstate 45 and Interstate 69/U.S. Highway 59 with direct access to the Hardy Toll Road expressway, George Bush Intercontinental Airport has scheduled flights to a large number of domestic and international destinations covering five continents. It is the second busiest airport in Texas for international passenger traffic as of 2025 (behind DFW) and has a number of international destinations, the second-busiest airport in Texas as of 2021 and the 15th busiest in the United States for total passenger traffic as of 2022.

IAH covers 10,000 acres (40 km2) of land and has five runways. Houston Intercontinental is one of the largest passenger hubs for United Airlines and formerly also served as a hub for one of United Airlines' predecessors, Continental Airlines, as well as defunct airlines Eastern Air Lines and Texas International Airlines."

description:
Changi Airport Terminal 1-2-3 Transit Area | Inside Best Airport In The World | Singapore Airport

Singapore Changi Airport, located in the Changi district at the eastern end of Singapore, is a major international airport and one of the largest transportation hubs in Asia. It’s approximately 24 kilometres (15 miles) east from Singapore’s Downtown Core. The airport comprises four terminals and Jewel Changi, a ten-storey lifestyle hub that seamlessly links to Terminals 1, 2, and 3. More than 100 airlines operate from the airport, with nonstop or direct flights to destinations in Asia, Oceania, Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and North America. It has been rated as the “World’s Best Airport” by Skytrax a dozen times and was the first airport in the world to hold the accolade for eight consecutive years. In 2019, Changi Airport served 68.3 million passengers, making it the 18th busiest airport in the world. Post Covid-19 pandemic, 58.9 million passengers passed through Changi Airport in 2023, rebounding to 86 per cent of traffic levels seen pre-pandemic. Changi Airport offers a trove of exciting activities, from shopping and dining to entertainment. It’s a world-class service icon and destination in itself.

title: Christmas 2022 @ Changi Airport | Tour of Singapore Changi Airport Jewel
description:
Christmas 2022@ Changi Airport |  Tour of Singapore Changi Airport Jewel

Jewel Changi Airport (also known as Jewel or Jewel Changi) is a nature-themed entertainment and retail complex surrounded by and linked to Changi Airport, Singapore, linked to one of its passenger terminals. Its centrepiece is the world's tallest indoor waterfall, the Rain Vortex, that is surrounded by a terraced forest setting.

Jewel includes gardens, attractions, a hotel, about 300 retail and dining outlets, as well as early baggage check-in aviation facilities. It covers a total gross floor area of 135,700 m2 (1,461,000 sq ft), spanning 10 storeys – five above-ground and five basement levels.Its attractions include the Shiseido Forest Valley, an indoor garden spanning five storeys, and the Canopy Park at the topmost level, featuring gardens and leisure facilities.

Jewel receives about 300,000 visitors per day. In October 2019, six months after its soft opening, it had welcomed 50 million visitors, exceeding its initial target for the whole year. The complex and airport is located in Changi, at the eastern end of Singapore, approximately 20 km (12 mi) northeast from Singapore's Downtown Core.

This time of evening walk in Paris, I met a heavy rain while I was moving around the Louvre Museum (Musée du Louvre) and I could capture Paris mood in the rain from the Louvre, Pont des Arts, the Seine river, and Pont neuf. Walking started in the avenue de l'opera that is situated in the center of the city, running northwest from the Louvre to the Palais Garnier, the primary opera house of Paris and then moved to the Louvre to film the feeling of standing at the very heart of French culture at an unusual time of day. The stroll continues to Paris famous bridges, Pont des Arts and Pont neuf, along the seine river. The path of the walk gives you an opportunity to visit and discover traditional and beautiful places in Paris.

Apologies for the spots on the lens and wind noises. I did several takes of this video, and by this one I had a lot of residue on the lens because of the heavy rain.

If you enjoyed this video, please LIKE and share it! Don't forget to subscribe to Paris Traveler channel for more walking tour videos and ambient sounds for sleep or meditation. Thank you for watching!

Date recorded: September, 2020
Weather: 🌧 14C | 57F

Lebanon 2026 4K Drone, 1 Hour Scenic and Soothing Relaxation Aerial Drone Film and Video in 4K and 8K for stress relief of Lebanon (لُبْنَان 2026) with Beirut (بيروت 2026), Batroun, Baalbek, Sannine Mountain, Sayidat Al Qarn, Aaqoura ; piano music, classical music, ambient music, meditation, yoga, zen, calming music, working music, study music, nature, relaxing.

Lebanon (or لُبْنَان in Arabic 2026) is a country in the Middle East and part of the Levant. Lebanon like Syria was strongly Hellenized during the ancient and Byzantine medieval times (Greek Orthodox). After the conquest of the Arabs the country became partly Islamized but it still has a strong Christian presence. Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate saw the emergence of the monastic orthodox traditions of the Maronites, and later of the Druze. This led to the Maronite-Druz dualism of Lebanon which is still present today. Lebanon is famous for its Cedar trees which are known as the Cedars of God. The cedar is the symbol of Lebanon and also represented in the Lebanese Flag. Lebanon is a country of 6 million people. Many of the Lebanese live in Beirut. The metropolitan area of Beirut has a population of 2,2 million.

On 4 August 2020, a massive explosion in the Port of Beirut resulted in the death of hundreds of people and destroyed the harbour and a huge part of the city. As many as 300,000 people have been left homeless by the explosion. The explosion was followed up by a huge fire in the city in September 2020. The cause of the blast is believed to be from stored ammonium nitrate. However, Beirut is rising from its ashes.

Music By Matteo de Grandis, Thomas Enger and Sarah Watson.

Welcome to Earth Relaxation !
Portugal, officially the Portuguese Republic, is a country whose mainland is located on the Iberian Peninsula of Southwestern Europe, and whose territory also includes the Atlantic archipelagos of the Azores and Madeira. Portugal is the westernmost point of Europe and lies on the west coast of the Iberian Peninsula. The long Atlantic coastline is popular with visitors and locals alike. Surfers are drawn to the strong surf in the west, and the warm, sandy beaches in the south are a haven for tourists. Lisbon, the national capital, was founded not by Celts but by the ancient Greek warrior Odysseus, who was said to have arrived at a rocky headland near what is the present-day city after leaving his homeland to wander the world and who, liking what he saw, stayed there for a while; his departure was said to have broken the heart of the nymph Calypso, who, the legend goes, turned herself into a snake, her coils becoming the seven hills of Lisbon. Climate, through its effect on vegetation, divides Portugal. As in Spain, three sets of influences are involved: Atlantic, continental (Mesetan), and Mediterranean. The Atlantic climate predominates overall, putting most of the country into the humid zone of the Iberian Peninsula; this is especially true in the northwest, where the climate is mild and rainy.

富士山　一周　富士五湖　春　ドライブ

Go around Mt.Fuji while visiting the 5 surrounding lakes. (circuit road 100km)
Mount Fuji looks symmetrical, but its shape changes depending on the viewing direction.
Young leaves are sprouting from the trees at the foot of the mountain, and the temperature in the city exceeds 30 degrees, but there is still a lot of snow on Mt. Fuji.

Mt.Fuji is 100km from the city center and takes about 2 hours.
Climbing takes a bus to the 5th Station (under the snow) and takes about 6 hours to reach the summit.
There is no snow in July and August, so you can enjoy it without worry.

There are five lakes on the north side (Yamanashi Prefecture, mountain side), and tourism is popular.
Dairy farming is thriving on the south side (sea side of Shizuoka Prefecture), and there are many grasslands and auto-camping grounds, and music festivals are also held.

title: 🚴 Scenic Cycling Journey from Brixen to Kiens | 4K GoPro POV | No Music, Just Nature
description:
#SlowTV #VirtualCycling #dolomites
Take a peaceful 1 hour 46 minute virtual bike ride through the breathtaking landscapes of South Tyrol, Italy — filmed on June 1, 2025, under a clear blue sky. This slow-paced e-bike ride starts in the charming old town of Brixen and follows the Pustertal Cycle Path all the way to Kiens, capturing the calm rhythm of nature, scenic riversides, historic landmarks, and mountain views.

🎥 Filmed in 5.3K on a GoPro mounted on the handlebar, exported in crisp 4K UHD for a truly immersive slow TV experience. No music, just the natural ambience — wind, tires, birdsong, and the occasional ripple of the river.

- Virtual cycling sessions on your exercise bike or treadmill

- Exploring South Tyrol from your couch

title: POV: Driving the Most Beautiful Roads in the Atlantic 🌊 [4K]
description:
Take a drive through some of the most dramatic landscapes in the Atlantic. 🌊 This route starts in the quiet, terraced valley of Boaventura, winding through narrow village backroads and passing the historic Solar de Boaventura before the scenery completely shifts.

Experience the thrill of Madeira's famous coastal roads, from rockfall-prone cliffside passes to the Duarte Pacheco tunnel. As we climb into the Queimadas laurel forest, the rain brings out the scent of eucalyptus before we head back down to Ponta Delgada to catch the sunset at Fajã da Areia. 🌅✨

title: 24 Hour Pakistani Street Food Tour | Epic Food Journeys with Mark Wiens | National Geographic
description:
Lahore is the undisputed food capital of Pakistan and Mark Wiens is ready to spend 24-hours taking it all in. Lahoris don't just love food, they're obsessed with it. From the chaos of Old Lahore to street grills and mango stalls packed with locals looking for a delicious respite from the heat, Mark encounters a city where food is fiery, portions are big, and passions run deep.

Beginning his Pakistani food journey at 4:30 AM, Mark travels to Haneef Siri Paye, a Lahore breakfast institution, known for paye, a dish consisting of braised goat feet served with freshly baked bread.

From there, Mark meets with Adil Lahorei, a passionate food lover and tour guide, to discover Old Lahore. They consume the famous Lahore street food snacks like Laohrei fruit chaat, which is made of bananas, apples, and apriciot sauce seasoned with masala, and dahi bhally, lentil fritters, potatoes, and yogurt seasoned with masala and chili.

Traveling on a colorful truck, Mark heads to the next spot, a famous pitstop designed restaurant at the Haji Usman Khan Hotel. There, he eats mutton rosh, slow cooked mutton, dal maash, yellow lentils stewed with black pepper and green chili, and Kabuli pulao -- fluffy rice, cooked with sweet carrots and bone marrow.

Continuing the trek through Lahore, Mark goes to Butt Karahi, a restaurant best known for the dish incorporated in its name, karahi (a rounded cooking pan) of fresh rooster simmered in with cream, butter, a variety of spices, and lots of green chilies and ginger.

Dairy is a huge part of the Punjab culture and Fazal Milk and Lassi Shop is famous for their Pairoo Wali Lassi, a massive cup of yogurt and cream, hand blended with milk fudge and topped with delicious butter balls.

With the day winding down, Mark tries takatak, one of the great Pakistani street foods that is named for the rhythmic clanking of the iron spatulas on the iron griddle. Then, at the Al Riaz Cafe, Mark chooses his won goat organs and passes them to the chef so they can mask everything up and season with spices and green chiles.

Looking for a cooling snack to survive a hot evening in Lahore, Mark goes to Heera Thandhe Amm to enjoy the prized chaunsa mangos cooled in an ice bath.

For late night Pakistani street food in Lahore, there are few things better than Ilyas Dumba Karahi (Truckaa Wala Adda). Mark meets up with longtime friend and food lover Ali Naqi Hamdani, to eat mutton karahi -- big chunks of fresh mutton cooked in a karahi over open fires with green chilies and black pepper.

Throughout the course of 24-hours, Mark Wiens has seen that Lahore is a city where you can eat like a king!

A sunny summer walk through the historic heart of Prague — from the modern Masaryčka and Old Town to Charles Bridge, Malá Strana and the Wallenstein Garden. 🇨🇿☀️

This immersive Prague walking tour in 4K passes many of the city’s essential sights, including the Powder Tower, Old Town Square, Prague Astronomical Clock, Karlova Street, Charles Bridge, the Čertovka canal and the Kafka Museum.

I filmed it during a spontaneous one-day trip in summer 2026: an early train from Dresden, roughly two hours to Prague, and a FlixBus back that evening. The weather stayed beautifully sunny with light clouds and temperatures around 27°C. The streets were lively, but still calmer than Prague can become during the busiest part of summer.

🎧 No narration and no added music — only authentic Prague ambience, footsteps, trams, conversations and city sounds.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

What does Leipzig feel like on a hot summer Saturday? Join this full-length 4K walking tour through the heart of Leipzig, Germany, filmed in bright sunshine at around 29°C / 84°F. 🇩🇪☀️

The 1 hour 43 minute walk begins at Augustusplatz and explores Leipzig’s lively city center at street level. We follow busy shopping streets, enter historic arcades and modern malls, pass packed restaurant terraces and discover landmarks including Leipzig Opera, the City-Hochhaus, Specks Hof, the Old Stock Exchange, Mädler Passage, Market Square, the Old Town Hall and St. Thomas Church.

The route continues through Petersstraße, Messehof Passage, Reichsstraße and Höfe am Brühl before ending at Willy-Brandt-Platz with a view of Leipzig Central Station. This is not an empty-city walk: it captures the authentic atmosphere of a popular German city on a sunny August weekend.

Watch it as virtual travel, use it to plan a Leipzig city trip or enjoy more than 100 minutes of real urban ambience on a big TV, computer or phone.

🎧 No narration and no added music – only authentic street sounds, conversations, shops, restaurants and city ambience recorded during the walk.

title: Monaco-Ville (Old Town), Prince's Palace - 🇲🇨 Monaco [4K HDR] Walking Tour
description:
Walking around Monaco-Ville, the historical part of Monaco City sightseeing the Prince's Palace of Monaco. Click here ▶ to see highlights and guide.

Monaco-Ville Old Town is very picturesque and is located on a hill that is surrounded on three sides by the Mediterranean. Once you get to the top you’ll find yourself in the Place du Palais in front of the Prince’s Palace of Monaco. The palace belongs to the current prince of Monaco, Albert II. The building is open to visitors, and tickets can be bought at the box office in front of the palace.

The square in front of the palace is spacious and provides a view of Monaco’s port and the buildings running up to the Monte Carlo district. A good eye will even be able to see the famous Monte Carlo Casino. The inner Old Town is built of charming, narrow streets that dates back to the 13th century when the principality was founded.

description:
Indulge in this curated 4K, 60fps walking tour of UNESCO's Pompeii archaeological area, Italy, featuring the ancient city's stunningly preserved ruins and historical landmarks 🎧 Best with headphones for an immersive experience (ASMR - Binaural City Sound). ⬇ LINKS to the full videos, chapters, etc. ⬇ Set beneath the shadow of Mount Vesuvius, Pompeii’s ancient streets hold a timeless allure. Once a bustling Roman city, it met an untimely end with the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 A.D., which preserved its buildings, artwork, and even daily life in a stunning, ash-covered tomb. Hidden beneath layers of ash for over 1,500 years, it was rediscovered in the 18th century, unveiling an extraordinary snapshot of the past. Today, Pompeii is one of Italy’s most famous archaeological sites, a mesmerizing destination that reveals the grandeur of Roman life frozen in time. title: British Columbia | Canada's Most Beautiful Province | Travel Documentary 4K
description:
Wonders of British Columbia | Canada's Most Beautiful Province | Travel Documentary 4K

Explore British Columbia from the Pacific Ocean to the Canadian Rockies in stunning 4K.

Hit that subscribe button—it’s completely free and really motivates me to create more content:https://www.youtube.com/@PathfindersTravel-YT?sub_confirmation=1

Between the Pacific Ocean and the Rocky Mountains lies British Columbia, Canada's most beautiful province. Join us on this travel documentary as we explore the Wonders of British Columbia revealing ancient temperate rainforests, glacial peaks, and wild coastlines. This BC travel guide takes you through 21 spectacular locations showcasing why British Columbia is one of the best places to visit in Canada. From Vancouver Island wilderness to Canadian Rockies alpine heights, this Canada travel documentary captures BC nature in stunning 4K quality.

VANCOUVER CITY
Downtown Vancouver blends urban sophistication with mountain views. Stanley Park protects ancient forests. English Bay offers sunset vistas where this BC travel guide begins.

SHANNON FALLS & SQUAMISH REGION
Shannon Falls cascades 335 meters along the Sea-to-Sky Highway. Stawamus Chief granite monolith towers above Squamish. Howe Sound Fjord creates dramatic British Columbia coastal landscapes.

GARIBALDI & JOFFRE LAKES
Garibaldi Lake shines turquoise beneath glaciated peaks. Panorama Ridge reveals 360-degree BC nature views. Lower Joffre Lake displays brilliant turquoise waters showcasing the Wonders of British Columbia.

WHISTLER REGION
Whistler Village sits at the base of Whistler Mountain and Blackcomb Peaks. This world-famous Whistler Canada resort demonstrates mountains rising from sea level to alpine heights.

BRANDYWINE FALLS & SETON LAKE
Brandywine Falls plunges 70 meters into volcanic canyon. Seton Lake's turquoise waters reflect surrounding peaks revealing hidden British Columbia beauty.

SUNSHINE COAST
Bonniebrook Beach, Sechelt, and Roberts Creek showcase BC's accessible coastal paradise in this travel documentary.

GREAT BEAR RAINFOREST
Spirit Bear Habitat protects the rare white Kermode bear. The Great Bear Rainforest represents Earth's last intact coastal temperate rainforest demonstrating the Wonders of British Columbia.

HAIDA GWAII & TOFINO
Bonanza Beach on Haida Gwaii features wild Pacific coastline. Pacific Rim National Park Reserve and Clayoquot Sound surround Tofino creating Vancouver Island's most spectacular wilderness in this Canada travel documentary.

VANCOUVER ISLAND REGION
Nanaimo Mountain and Harbor represent Vancouver Island's eastern gateway showing diverse British Columbia landscapes.

CANADIAN ROCKIES PARKS
Mount Revelstoke National Park features alpine meadows. Marble Canyon cuts through Kootenay National Park limestone. Takakkaw Falls thunders 373 meters in Yoho National Park. Mount Robson Peak rises 3,954 meters as the Canadian Rockies highest summit where Fraser River begins.

OKANAGAN VALLEY
Kalamalka Lake changes colors creating Okanagan Valley magic. Kelowna anchors wine country. Okanagan Lake stretches through Penticton and Wine Country Vineyards showing interior British Columbia beauty in this travel documentary.

FRASER VALLEY REGION
Fraser Canyon and Harrison Lake represent the agricultural heartland connecting coast to interior British Columbia.

This travel documentary reveals how British Columbia transformed from frontier wilderness into Canada's most spectacular province. From Vancouver to Haida Gwaii, from Vancouver Island to the Canadian Rockies, from Whistler Canada to Okanagan Valley, British Columbia defies expectation. The Wonders of British Columbia include spirit bears, ancient cedars, and landscapes that showcase why this is the ultimate BC travel guide. This BC nature documentary captures the province through stunning 4K cinematography.

title: Istanbul 4K 🇹🇷 Galataport Walking Tour | Luxury Shopping, Brands, Restaurants & Bosphorus
description:
Istanbul 4K Galataport Walking Tour in Istanbul, Turkey — explore luxury shopping, international brands, waterfront restaurants, Bosphorus views and one of Istanbul’s most popular modern travel destinations.

Take an immersive summer walk through Galataport Istanbul, a modern waterfront destination on Istanbul’s European side. This 4K walking tour begins inside the Galataport shopping and lifestyle complex, following a main indoor passage through international brands and retail spaces before reaching the Bosphorus waterfront.

Continue along the waterfront promenade with views of restaurants, cafes, the Bosphorus and Galataport’s modern architecture. We then reach the main Galataport square and its striking red architectural installation featuring the names of countries and destinations from around the world.

The walk continues inside the shopping center, exploring more luxury brands and retail spaces before going upstairs for a different view over the square. We then return downstairs and pass the historic Nusretiye Mosque before continuing toward Galataport Saat Kulesi Meydanı and its historic Clock Tower.

From the Clock Tower Square, the route returns toward the waterfront and continues in the opposite direction along the Galataport promenade. We then enter the indoor shopping area again, see the İş Bankası ship, explore the interior, and finish this Istanbul walking tour.

Galataport is located in a historic part of Istanbul where the modern waterfront meets the heritage of Karaköy and Tophane. The area is close to Galata Tower, Karaköy, Kabataş and Taksim, while Eminönü, the Galata Bridge and the historic peninsula are also within easy reach. Official Galataport information lists Karaköy and Kabataş piers among the main access points, with Eminönü and other central Istanbul districts connected by public transport and short walking routes.

For travelers planning a Turkey vacation, Galataport can be combined with a wider Istanbul itinerary including Karaköy and Galata Tower, walking across Galata Bridge toward Eminönü and the Spice Bazaar, exploring Taksim and Istiklal Street, or continuing along the Bosphorus toward Beşiktaş and other waterfront neighborhoods.

The surrounding area also reflects Istanbul’s layered history. Karaköy and the Galata waterfront have been important parts of the city for centuries, while historic landmarks around Galataport include Nusretiye Mosque, Tophane Clock Tower, Tophane Fountain and restored heritage buildings such as the historic Post Office.

title: 🇹🇷 Istanbul Turkey 2026 4K Walking Tour | Vezneciler to Süleymaniye & Eminönü Bazaar
description:
''🇹🇷 Istanbul Turkey 2026 4K Walking Tour | Vezneciler to Süleymaniye & Eminönü Bazaar''

Let's explore together the vibrant heart of Istanbul, Turkey with 'Walking Vitamin' in another virtual tour and video. Join us as we embark on a captivating journey to 'Vezneciler' then 'Suleymaniye' and finally 'Eminonu', capturing the lively streets, bustling markets, and historic places.

Located in the Fatih district, one of Istanbul’s oldest and most iconic areas, 'Vezneciler' is a blend of traditional charm and modern energy. As we walk through its lively streets, you’ll experience the blend of Ottoman history and contemporary life that makes this area so special and feel the vibrant atmosphere around Istanbul University.

As we continue our route, we reach to 'Süleymaniye' neighborhood and the grand magnicifant Süleymaniye Mosque. The Süleymaniye Mosque (Turkish: Süleymaniye Camii) is an Ottoman imperial mosque located on the Third Hill of Istanbul, Turkey. The mosque was commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent and designed by the imperial architect Mimar Sinan. Behind the qibla wall of the mosque is an enclosure containing the separate octagonal mausoleums of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hurrem Sultan (Roxelana). For 462 years, the Süleymaniye Mosque was the largest mosque in the city, until it was surpassed by the Çamlıca Mosque in 2019. The Süleymaniye Mosque is one of the best-known sights of Istanbul, and from its location on the Third Hill, it commands an extensive view of the city around the Golden Horn.

At the end we explore the colorful and delicious atmosphere of Eminönü Bazaar in Istanbul, Turkey, one of the most lively market areas in the historic Old City. Eminönü is located in the heart of Istanbul’s Old City, close to the Spice Bazaar, Grand Bazaar, Sirkeci, Galata Bridge, Karaköy, Sultanahmet, and the Golden Horn. This area is one of the best places to experience the real shopping culture of Istanbul, where locals and tourists come together for food, spices, sweets, souvenirs, clothes, fresh products, and street market atmosphere.

If your are still wondering what to see in Istanbul and where to go besides the most touristic places in Sultanahmet then this is another good option close to that area. title: 🇹🇷 Istanbul Turkey 4K Walking Tour 2026 | Ortaköy Kumpir Street, Soviniour Markets & Bosphorus Views

''🇹🇷 Istanbul Turkey 4K Walking Tour 2026 | Ortaköy Kumpir Street, Soviniour Markets & Bosphorus Views''

Welcome to our new captivating video, where we invite you to join us on an enchanting journey through 'Ortaköy', a picturesque neighborhood nestled along the Bosphorus in European side of Istanbul, Turkey. Ortaköy is one of Istanbul’s most iconic Bosphorus neighborhoods—famous for its waterfront atmosphere, lively square, and postcard views of the Ortaköy Mosque (Büyük Mecidiye Camii) with the Bosphorus Bridge in the background. In this ISTANBUL TURKEY 2026 4K WALKING TOUR, you’ll experience real street life in Ortaköy: crowds, seaside vibes, local shops, and the classic Istanbul mix of history, food, and scenery.

The area is world-famous because it is located within a triangle of historical religions. The Ortaköy Mosque, Ayios Fokas Church and Etz Ahayim Synagogue make up the triangle, one of the most characteristic neighbourhoods in Istanbul. Many travelers search online for “Ortaköy Istanbul things to do,” “Ortaköy Mosque view,” “Bosphorus photo spots,” “best Bosphorus neighborhood,” and “Ortaköy nightlife/cafes.” This walk is designed to show exactly what visitors want to see before they go—how the area feels in real life, where the action is, and what makes Ortaköy a top stop for tourists exploring the Bosphorus line.

If you’re looking for Istanbul street food, Ortaköy is a must for quick bites by the water. Along the way you’ll see street food (kumpir, waffles, mussels), boutique shops, local prices, and everyday moments that define Istanbul’s vibe in May 2026. Filmed in 4K 60FPS with natural city sounds for an immersive feel—perfect for virtual travel and trip planning.

Getting to Ortaköy is straightforward with Istanbul public transport: buses and dolmuş lines run along the coast and connect from major points like Beşiktaş and Kabataş (use Istanbulkart). The area is best explored on foot, especially along the waterfront. title: Rome, Italy 🇮🇹 - 2022 - 4K HDR Walking Tour (▶558 min)
description:
This video of Rome Was filmed in January of 2022.
Rome has no rivals when it comes to beauty, history, art, nature, parks, architecture and monumentality. The city changes continuously, offering all possible architectural styles which often overlaps, creating two, often three or four level structures that might incorporate, for example, a baroque palace underneath which there might be a medieval church beneath which you might have a second century church under which there might be 3 levels of ancient catacombs.
Additionally, the city displays the greatest amount of monuments and/or points of interest among all world cities, having about 15% of the entire world’s artistic/historic/archaeological/architectural/ inheritance. That is one-sixth of the world’s treasures condensed in one city.
From skyscrapers to rationalism to neoclassicism to Art Deco to Renaissance to Baroque to Medieval to Neo-Gothic to imperial Rome…the list never ends.
I cannot even begin to write about the Eternal City, so much is there.

Here are 12 interesting facts about Rome.

Modern Rome has 280 fountains and more than 900 churches.
Nearly 700,000 euros worth of coins are tossed into Rome’s Trevi Fountain each year. The proceeds are donated to Caritas to help those in need.
The Romans had built a road network of 53,000 miles by the early fourth century. Each Roman mile was about 4,800 feet and marked by a milestone, giving birth to the saying “All roads lead to Rome.”
In Ancient Rome, only free-born men were allowed to wear togas, a sign of Roman citizenship. Women wore stolas, the female version of togas, made from linen.
The mascot of Rome is a she-wolf that cared for brothers Romulus and Remus, the mythological founders of Rome.
Rome became the capital city of unified Italy in 1870, taking the title from Florence.
Law in Rome allows cats to live without disruption in the place they were born. Wild cats can be climbing the walls of the Colosseum, and sleeping among the ruins of the Forum.
Women in ancient Rome dyed their hair with goat fat and beech wood ashes. The most popular colors were red and blond.
The first ever shopping mall was built in Rome between 107 and 110 AD by Emperor Trajan. It sold a wide variety of goods and grocery items.
Rome’s first university, La Sapienza, established in 1303 AD, is the largest in Europe and the second largest in the world.
Rome has a museum dedicated entirely to pasta.
St Peter’s basilica inside Vatican City is the largest church ever constructed.

Explore the lively atmosphere of Venice Beach, one of the most famous beachfront neighborhoods in Los Angeles. Venice Beach is also known for its skate park, street murals, palm-lined ocean views, and vibrant coastal lifestyle, making it one of the most photographed and visited destinations in Los Angeles.

description:
Experience a Real Istanbul 4K Walk starting at the BUSTLING Eminonu Bazaar with Walk With Me in Turkey. Enjoy authentic street food, fish sandwich boats, and a magical Galata Bridge sunset overlooking the Golden Horn & Metro view. Walk With Me in Turkey brings you the most immersive city tours.

This immersive walking tour takes you through the heart of Istanbul's most vibrant district. We begin in the chaotic energy of Eminonu Square and the Spice Bazaar area, weaving through crowds of locals and tourists with Walk With Me in Turkey. Witness the famous floating fish sandwich boats (Balık Ekmek) before crossing the historic Galata Bridge. The video concludes with a breathtaking panoramic view of the Haliç Metro Bridge and the Golden Horn skyline during the golden hour, capturing the true soul of the city with Walk With Me in Turkey.

🏛️ About the Locations in this Tour
Eminönü & The Bazaars: Eminönü is the historic heart of Istanbul's trade. The Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı), dating back to 1660, is famous for its vibrant colors and exotic scents. Walking here with Walk With Me in Turkey, you feel the centuries of history in every corner.

Galata Bridge & The Fishermen: A symbol of Istanbul, the Galata Bridge connects the old city to the modern districts. It is legendary for the hundreds of local fishermen lining its rails day and night. Crossing this bridge with Walk With Me in Turkey offers a unique glimpse into the daily life of Istanbullus.

The Iconic Fish Sandwiches (Balık Ekmek): You haven't truly visited Eminonu until you've seen the traditional sultan-style boats preparing fresh Mackerel sandwiches. It is one of the world's most famous street food experiences, captured perfectly by Walk With Me in Turkey.

Haliç Metro Bridge & Train Views: The Haliç Metro Bridge station is an architectural wonder suspended right over the Golden Horn. In this episode of Istanbul Walking Tour, we explore the station's unique vantage points and capture the mesmerizing movement of the trains from above as they cross the bridge. Experience the perfect blend of modern transit and historic views with Istanbul Walking Tour, watching the metro pass by against the backdrop of the city's ancient skyline.

Discover the Peloponnese, the peninsula where ancient Greece actually happened. title: IRAN: Exploring The Hidden Beauty As An American Tourist | 4K Travel Documentary
description:
🎥Journey into Iran — where contradiction is not a flaw, but a system. In this cinematic 4K documentary, explore a nation shaped by pressure, resilience, and a cultural logic that allows life to continue under conditions most systems would fail to endure. From Tehran to Isfahan, Shiraz to Tabriz, Iran unfolds as a country living across multiple realities at once. Since early 2026, the sounds of conflict have echoed across the country — yet for millions, this is not disruption, but continuity. Witness how daily life persists through sanctions and instability — where adaptation replaces stability, and survival becomes a practiced system passed down through generations. From the Qashqai migration in the Zagros Mountains to the vertical village of Palangan, from the extremes of Ahvaz and Bandar Abbas to the paradox of Kish Island, each place reveals a different layer of this reality. And above it all stands Mount Damavand — where myth and geology coexist, and endurance becomes identity. This is not just Iran as a place. It is Iran as a system — of survival, contradiction, and continuity. A hidden world where nothing fully collapses, because everything adapts.

Singapore Changi Airport is a world-renowned aviation hub known for its exceptional service, state-of-the-art facilities, and vibrant attractions. Serving as a key gateway for international travelers, it boasts four terminals and the Jewel, a multi-use complex featuring the iconic Rain Vortex—the world’s tallest indoor waterfall—along with lush gardens, retail shops, and dining options. Recognized for its efficiency and innovation, Changi Airport consistently ranks among the best airports globally, offering seamless connectivity, luxurious lounges, and unique amenities such as movie theaters, swimming pools, and immersive art installations. It embodies Singapore’s commitment to excellence and hospitality, making it more than just a transit point but a destination in itself.


Singapore Changi Airport Terminal 1, one of the airport's four terminals, is a bustling hub that combines world-class facilities with seamless travel experiences. Opened in 1981, it has been modernized over the years to offer state-of-the-art amenities, including an extensive array of dining, shopping, and leisure options. The terminal is home to the iconic "Kinetic Rain" sculpture, a mesmerizing art installation that captivates travelers. Designed to handle both regional and long-haul flights, Terminal 1 serves major airlines and connects Singapore to numerous destinations worldwide. Its strategic layout ensures efficient passenger flow, making it a favorite among travelers for its convenience and comfort.

Singapore Changi Airport Terminal 2 is a bustling hub known for its efficient operations and passenger-friendly amenities. Opened in 1991, it caters to a wide range of international and regional flights, offering seamless connectivity for travelers. The terminal features modern facilities, including spacious lounges, diverse dining options, duty-free shopping, and relaxation areas designed to enhance the travel experience. Recent upgrades have introduced energy-efficient systems and refreshed interiors, maintaining its reputation as a world-class airport. Terminal 2 reflects Singapore's commitment to excellence in aviation and continues to serve millions of passengers annually with convenience and style.

Singapore Changi Airport Terminal 3 is a modern and spacious terminal known for its state-of-the-art facilities and stunning architecture. Opened in 2008, it features a distinctive roof with skylights that filter natural light into the terminal, creating a bright and welcoming ambiance. Terminal 3 boasts world-class amenities, including lush indoor gardens, luxury shopping outlets, diverse dining options, and innovative services like automated check-in kiosks and baggage handling systems. The terminal also houses the iconic "Green Wall," a vertical garden that spans over 300 meters, enhancing the terminal's eco-friendly appeal. With its seamless blend of functionality and aesthetics, Terminal 3 is a favorite among travelers for comfort and convenience.

Chinese New Year, also known as Lunar New Year, is one of the most significant celebrations in Singapore, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of its Chinese community. Typically held in late January or early February, the festival is marked by vibrant traditions and family gatherings. Streets in areas like Chinatown come alive with dazzling decorations, bustling markets, and festive performances, including lion dances and firecrackers, believed to bring good luck and ward off evil spirits. Families engage in spring cleaning, exchange mandarin oranges, and enjoy reunion dinners featuring symbolic dishes such as dumplings and yusheng. The holiday embodies themes of renewal, prosperity, and togetherness, making it a cherished time for all.

title: Istanbul 🇹🇷 Airport [ 4K ] Walking Tour
description:
Istanbul Airport: https://goo.gl/maps/5JEmkwNWyNyrLszi6

In this video, we take a walk through Istanbul Airport Havalimanı, exploring its vast terminals, modern facilities, and bustling atmosphere that make it one of the world's most prominent aviation hubs.

Istanbul Airport, also known as Istanbul Havalimanı in Turkish, is a major international airport located in Istanbul, Turkey. It is one of the largest and busiest airports in the world, serving as a key transportation hub connecting Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Istanbul Airport is located on the European side of Istanbul near the Black Sea coast, approximately 35 kilometers northwest of Istanbul's city center.

Istanbul Airport is one of the largest airports in the world in terms of total area. It spans over 76.5 million square meters, making it one of the largest single-building airports in the world. The airport has six runways, with the capacity to handle up to 500 takeoffs and landings per hour, and has the potential to serve more than 200 million passengers annually when fully completed.

The airport has a unique terminal design with a centralized layout. It has a main terminal building called the "Istanbul Airport Terminal," which is divided into three sections: Main Terminal, International Departures, and International Arrivals. The terminal is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities and amenities for passengers, including numerous check-in counters, security screening points, lounges, duty-free shops, restaurants, and other services.

Istanbul Airport offers a wide range of facilities and services to cater to the needs of passengers. These include numerous shops, restaurants, cafes, lounges, prayer rooms, children's play areas, baggage services, currency exchange, car rental services, medical services, and more. The airport is designed with modern architecture, advanced technology, and sustainability features to provide a seamless and enjoyable travel experience for passengers.

Overall, Istanbul Airport is a state-of-the-art international airport that plays a significant role in connecting the world with Turkey and serves as a major aviation hub in the region. With its modern facilities, extensive connectivity, and strategic location, it has become a major gateway for global travelers visiting Istanbul and beyond.

title: 4K 🇹🇭 Walking around Saphan Taksin Station and Sathorn Pier in Bangkok, Thailand 2023
description: This is the evening atmosphere around Saphan Taksin BTS Station and Sathorn Pier in Bangkok of Thailand. This area is located on Charoen krung road in Bangrak District of Bangkok. This street is near Sathon Pier where is many people take a boat cross the river to Icon Siam shopping center. Sathon pier is a major pier on the Chao Phraya River located beneath the Taksin Bridge. It is the main pier for the Chao Phraya Express Boat and MINE Smart Ferry with all services stopping at this pier. There is also a cross-river ferry service from the pier to Charoen Nakhon in Thonburi. Sathorn Pier is located adjacent to the Saphan Taksin Station, making this location the only place for commuters to transfer between the Chao Phraya Express Boat service and the Bangkok BTS Skytrain Silom Line rail service. This area is surrounded by shopping mall, Bangrak Bazaar, Shangri-La Hotel, restaurants and café. And also there are many Thai street food stalls sell on the sidewalk. This area is always busy with people walking past on the street. title: 🇹🇷 4K • 3D • İzmir Walking Tour | Most Iconic Landmarks
description: Welcome to Old Towns Are you ready to take a step into the heart of İzmir, through streets filled with history and the city's most elegant corners? Today, I grabbed my camera and walked a magnificent route starting from the historic streets of Basmane and extending step by step to Konak Square, with each corner holding a unique story. Without any voiceover or narration, accompanied only by the city's own natural melody and captivating views, we are taking a close look at 5 of İzmir's most iconic historical structures. Here are the 5 iconic places that make İzmir what it is, which we explored together on this walk: 🏛️ 1. The Iconic Basmane Train Station (Starting Point) Construction Date: 1866 (Year of opening) Purpose & History: Built as the starting point of the İzmir-Kasaba (Turgutlu) railway line to connect the region's trade directly to the port. The design was created by the office of the famous French architect Gustave Eiffel (or the prominent French architectural school of that era). Reflecting the industrial revolution's iron truss aesthetics and exquisite cut stone craftsmanship, it stands as İzmir's historic first gateway to Anatolia. 👞 2. The Iconic Kavaflar Bazaar (Shoemakers' Bazaar) Construction Date: 1929 Purpose & History: Built to revive the city's commerce after rising from the ashes of the Great Fire of İzmir in 1922. It was specifically designed to gather the city's shoemakers under one roof. As one of the first planned bazaar examples of the early Turkish Republic era, this two-story structure boasts a wonderful architectural aesthetic that brings the warmth of wood and stone to the present day. ☕ 3. The Iconic Kızlarağası Han (The Grand Bazaar) Construction Date: 1744 Purpose & History: Commissioned by Hacı Beşir Ağa, who served as the Grand Vizier and Chief Eunuch of the Ottoman Empire. Located close to the harbor, this traditional Ottoman caravanserai was designed for merchants arriving with camel caravans to lodge and trade their goods. Today, filled with the rich aroma of Turkish coffee brewing in its historic courtyard, it remains the vibrant heart of Kemeraltı. 🎭 4. The Iconic Alhambra Cinema (İzmir National Cinema) Construction Date: 1926 Purpose & History: Designed by the prominent architect Tahsin Sermet Bey in the style of the First National Architectural Movement. It was constructed to generate financial income for the İzmir National Library. With its beautiful Kütahya tiles on the facade, neoclassical structure, and magnificent interior ceiling decorations, it was the brightest cultural beacon of Republican-era İzmir. Today, it proudly hosts the State Opera and Ballet and the City Theaters. 🕰️ 5. The Iconic İzmir Clock Tower (Konak Square) Construction Date: 1901 Purpose & History: Built under the leadership of İzmir Governor Kıbrıslı Kamil Pasha to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II's accession to the throne. It was designed by the French-Levantine architect Raymond Charles Péré. The intricate clock mechanism was a personal gift from German Emperor Wilhelm II. The circular fountains at its base still bring refreshing life to the square. 00:00 - Preview 00:30 - Basmane - Fevzi Paşa Boulevard 11:11 - Gazi Osman Paşa Boulevard 13:35 - Kemeraltı 20:00 - Fevzi Paşa Boulevard 25:00 - Kızlarağası Hanı - Kemeraltı Bazaar 54:30 - Konak - Atatürk Square

description: Welcome to China's Most Beautiful Water Village. Join us on a serene and picturesque journey through Suzhou, China's in stunning 4K HDR 60fps quality. Video Highlights: Here are the highlights for Suzhou Water Village, one of China's most picturesque and culturally rich water towns: 1. **Pingjiang Road:** A historic street lined with traditional buildings, teahouses, and shops, offering a glimpse into the ancient lifestyle of Suzhou. 2. **Humble Administrator's Garden (Zhuo Zheng Yuan):** One of the most famous classical gardens in China, known for its beautiful ponds, rock formations, and traditional pavilions. 3. **Lingering Garden (Liu Yuan):** Another UNESCO World Heritage site, featuring exquisite landscaping, intricate architecture, and serene water features. 4. **Master of the Nets Garden (Wangshi Yuan):** A smaller yet beautifully designed garden, showcasing classical Chinese garden aesthetics. 5. **Suzhou Museum:** Designed by the renowned architect I.M. Pei, this museum houses a vast collection of ancient Chinese art, ceramics, and cultural artifacts. 6. **Tiger Hill (Hu Qiu):** A historic site with a leaning pagoda, ancient tombs, and beautiful landscapes, offering panoramic views of Suzhou. 7. **Shantang Street:** An ancient canal street bustling with traditional shops, restaurants, and cultural performances. 8. **Suzhou Silk Museum:** A museum dedicated to the history and art of silk production, showcasing exquisite silk garments and weaving techniques. 9. **Pan Gate (Pan Men):** A historic city gate and water gate, part of Suzhou's title: Discover Tirana, Albania 🇦🇱 in 4K HDR | Summer Walking Tour 60fps
description: Welcome to our 4K walking tour of Tirana, Albania! Join us as we explore the vibrant streets and hidden gems of this beautiful capital city during the summer. Immerse yourself in the lively atmosphere, rich history, and stunning architecture that Tirana has to offer. Skanderbeg Square: The central hub of Tirana, Skanderbeg Square is a vast plaza surrounded by important landmarks like the National History Museum, Opera House, and several government buildings. Named after the national hero, it is a focal point for cultural events and public gatherings. Blloku: Once a restricted area for the communist elite, Blloku is now a trendy district filled with cafes, bars, restaurants, and boutiques. Its colourful buildings and lively nightlife make it a favourite spot for both locals and tourists. Grand Park of Tirana: This expansive park is a green oasis in the city, featuring walking trails, a large artificial lake, and picnic areas. It's a perfect place to relax, enjoy nature, and escape the hustle and bustle of urban life. Ethem Bey Mosque and Clock Tower: These historic landmarks are located in the heart of Tirana. The Ethem Bey Mosque, built in the early 19th century, is renowned for its intricate frescoes and beautiful interior. The adjacent Clock Tower offers panoramic views of the city. Pyramid of Tirana: Originally built as a museum dedicated to Enver Hoxha, Albania's communist leader, the Pyramid has since become an iconic and somewhat controversial structure. Plans are underway to repurpose it as a multifunctional cultural centre. New Bazaar (Pazari i Ri): This vibrant market area has been revitalized with colourful stalls and modern amenities. It’s a great place to explore local produce, traditional foods, and handmade crafts, giving a taste of Albanian culture and hospitality. Modern Skyscrapers: Tirana is experiencing a construction boom with several new skyscrapers reshaping its skyline. These modern buildings blend innovative architecture with contemporary design, reflecting the city’s rapid development and growing economic dynamism. Notable projects include the Downtown One, a mixed-use tower that is set to become the tallest building in Albania, and the innovative design of the Tirana Business Park. 📍 Location: Tirana, Albania 📅 Season: Summer 2024 📷 Quality: 4K HDR In this video, you'll experience: Chapters: 0:00 Intro Preview 3:28 The bustling Skanderbeg Square, the heart of Tirana 12:14 The colourful facades and unique street art around Blloku 17:46 The Historical Fortress of Justinian & Market 30:44 The Great Ottoman Namazgah Mosque of Albania 34:41Balkan Adventure Street towards Market 43:44 Colourful New Bazaar (Pazari i Ri) 57:33 Bulevardi Zogu I Parë (Bulevardi Zogu I) 1:08:37 National Historical Museum 1:11:31 National Opera House 1: 14:12 Historic Ethem Bey Mosque and Clock Tower 1:16:02 Bunk'Art 2 Bunker Museum 1:21:00 Independence Monument & Park 1:28:34 Massive Communist Pyramid of Tirana 👍 Like this video if you enjoyed it! 💬 Comment below with your favourite part of the tour! 🔔 Subscribe for more walking tours and travel content! The palace complex has hundreds of rooms and chambers, but only the most important are accessible to the public as of 2021. title: 🇨🇦 Montreal Walking Tour - Old Montreal Quebec Canada Walkthrough [4K Ultra HDR/60fps]
description: Two hour walking tour of Downtown Montreal. Montreal is the second-most populous city in Canada, and most populous city in the Canadian province of Quebec. Montreal is one of the most bilingual cities in Canada, with over 59% of the population able to speak both English and French. Our walk starts in front of Notre Dame Basilica in the historic district of Old Montreal, in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. The church is next to the Saint-Sulpice Seminary and faces the monument in memory of Paul de Chomedey, founder of Montreal in Place d'Armes square. Leaving the square, we make our way down the cobblestone roads towards Montréals famous Crew Collective Cafe. This café is undeniably among the most beautiful spots in all of Montreal. Located in the venerable and grand former headquarters of the Royal Bank of Canada – once the tallest building in the British Empire – in the heart of Old Montreal, the high ceilings, marble floors and brass cashier counters will surely blow you away. Leaving the soaring ceilings of Crew Cafe, we head towards Rue Saint-Paul Street, the oldest street in Montreal, and one of the most picturesque in the city. Paved in 1672, the cobblestone artery is home to many historic greystone buildings, which are emblematic of Montreal. While walking down Saint-Paul Street, you’ll encounter all manner of shops, galleries and restaurants. It is also a pleasure just to stroll down the narrow street, which runs parallel to the Old Port waterfront. Eventually, you’ll hit Place Jacques-Cartier, a square named after the eponymous explorer who claimed Canada for France in 1535. The Sailors Church officially named Notre-Dame-de-Bon-Secours Chapel ("Our Lady of Good Help") is one of the oldest churches in Montreal, it was built in 1771 over the ruins of an earlier chapel. The church is located at 400 Saint Paul Street East at Bonsecours Street, just north of the Bonsecours Market in the borough of Ville-Marie (Champ-de-Mars metro station). The Old Port of Montreal (French: Vieux-Port de Montréal) is the historic port of Quebec that dates well before the formation of Canada. Located adjacent to Old Montreal, it stretches for over 2 km (1.2 mi) along the Saint Lawrence River. It was used as early as 1611, when French fur traders used it as a trading post. Quartier des Spectacles is an arts and entertainment district located in the eastern section of Downtown Montreal, designed as a centre for Montreal's cultural events and festivals. The Quartier des spectacles is a member of the Global Cultural Districts Network. With a total area of almost one square kilometre, the Quartier is bounded by City Councillors Street to the West, Berri Street to the East, Sherbrooke Street to the North and René Lévesque Boulevard to the South, encompassing all of the district known as Montreal's Latin Quarter. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Chapters: 0:00 Preview 7:09 Notre-Dame Basilica 20:20 Crew Collective Cafe 34:40 Place d'Armes Square 43:20 Rue Saint-Paul Street 57:48 Place Jacques-Cartier 1:10:30 Marché Bonsecours 1:16:00 The Sailors Church 1:27:00 Vieux-Port Montréal 1:29:45 The Ferris Wheel 1:38:11 Boardwalk to Sailors Tower 1:45:50 Quatier des Festivals 2:06:30 Place des Arts 2:16:06 Complexe Desjardins ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Let's connect: ►Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/c/4KWanderings ►Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/4kWanderings ►Twitter: https://twitter.com/17NorthNE ►Instagram: https://instagram.com/17NNE ►TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@microwalks Intro music produced by Ryan Booth at The JamBooth Recording Studio. https://thejambooth.wixsite.com/music https://facebook.com/JamBoothMusic/ #Montreal #Canada #Walkingtour #4kvideo #oldmontreal

title: 🇲🇽 Mexico City, Mexico 4K Walking Tour - Historic City Center Tour | 4K Ultra HD / 60fps
description: Welcome to the Historic Centre of Mexico City. Todays walking tour is approximately 1 hour. We start todays walk at the Palacio de Bellas Artes, one of the cities prominent cultural centres and iconic images of the Country. The exterior of the building is primarily Art Nouveau and Neoclassical and the interior is primarily Art Deco. The building is best known for its murals by Diego Rivera, Siqueiros and others, as well as the many exhibitions and theatrical performances it hosts, including the Ballet Folklórico de México. Walking through the plaza we find our way towards passed the Casa de los Azulejos or "House of Tiles", which we will visit later on in our tour. Passing the blue tile walls we enter a sculpture garden. Walking further down Madero Ave, we pass street vendors and basic taquerías side by side with high-end restaurants and boutiques. All along this bustling, pedestrian-only street we find some of the cities oldest historic landmarks, some dating from as far back as the Aztec era. Reaching the end of the pedestrian mall, we enter Zócalo plaza, the city's beating heart. The area draws tourists to museums and iconic buildings like The Metropolitan Cathedral of the Assumption of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary into Heaven, a grand cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Mexico. Heading away from the square, we aim ourselves towards the Torre Latinoamericana, one of the cities first skyscrapers in downtown Mexico City. Its central location, height, and history make it one of the city's most important landmarks. Once we circle back down along Mexico Cities 5th Ave, we find ourselves back at The House of Tiles. The iconic blue building is an 18th-century Baroque palace in Mexico City, built by the Count of the Valle de Orizaba family. The building is distinguished by its facade, which is covered on three sides by blue and white tile of Puebla state. We follow our way back passed the Palacio de Bellas Artes and into Mexico Cities China Town, known as Barrio Chino. The neighbourhood is located on two blocks of Dolores Street and consists of many Chinese styled restaurants, businesses, and import goods stores. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Intro music produced by Ryan Booth at The JamBooth Recording Studio. https://thejambooth.wixsite.com/music​ https://facebook.com/JamBoothMusic/ #mexico #mexicocity #walkingtour #4kwalk #travel #mexico2024

title: 🇪🇬 Dahab, Egypt Walking Tour of Beach Main Road [4K HD / 60 FPS]
description: Todays walking tour is approximately 1 hour. Dahab is a recently developed, very liberal Egyptian town on the southeast coast of the Sinai Peninsula. Formerly a Bedouin fishing spot, Dahab is now considered to be one of Egypt's most treasured diving destinations. Dahab can be divided into three major parts. Masbat, which includes the Bedouin village Asalah, is in the north. South of Masbat is Mashraba, which is more touristic and has considerably more hotels. In the southwest is Medina which includes the Laguna area, famous for its excellent shallow-water windsurfing. Dahab attracts large numbers of tourists. It is world-renowned for its windsurfing. Reliable winds provide superb flat-water conditions inside Dahab's sand spit. Further away from shore, wavy conditions couple with strong winds to provide formidable conditions for keen windsurfers. However, in recent years, the lagoon inside the sand spit has been overtaken by kitesurfers, with two Russian-owned schools opening right on the beach. SCUBA diving, free-diving and snorkelling are also popular activities with many reefs immediately adjacent to waterfront hotels. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Intro music produced by Ryan Booth at The JamBooth Recording Studio. https://thejambooth.wixsite.com/music​ https://facebook.com/JamBoothMusic/ #walkingtour #streetlife #4kwalk #dahab #egypt #beachlife

title: 🇨🇦 Montreal Walking Tour - Street Life in Downtown Montreal [4K HDR 60fps]
description: This week we're walking the Pedestrian Streets of Montréal. Pedestrian streets are particularly popular in Montréal, and are part of their unique urban landscape. Montréal's colourful streets encourage people to connect with places, and ensure the vibrancy of neighbourhoods and their businesses. The increased safety of pedestrian streets is also a big plus. With cars prohibited or tightly controlled, pedestrians feel much safer and the risk of accidents is much lower. Nuisances caused by vehicle traffic, such as stress and air and noise pollution, are also greatly reduced. Finally, the more spacious layout of these streets allows each walker to choose his or her own pace, regardless of physical condition, and encourages active mobility. The city is capitalizing on the great potential of local streets to create new neighbourhood public places where people can meet. Converting streets to pedestrian malls is part of this process and encourages appropriation of public spaces, discovery of local neighbourhoods and interactions between those who make them come alive. Montreal Mayor Valérie Plante has announced that 10 streets in the city will be pedestrian-only this summer. Montréal is a great city for walking and enjoying public places. The city will provide $12-million in funding for the pedestrianization of the commercial arteries spread over a three-year period. Pedestrian and shared-use streets, whether permanent or seasonal, provide a safe, enjoyable walking environment in the heart of the city. These colourful streets have become a signature and a staple of summer in Montreal. Try one out and you’ll discover new meeting places and opportunities for relaxation and entertainment in the heart of your favourite neighbourhoods. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Chapters: 0:00 Intro 4:00 Place Émilie-gamelin 58:05 Plateau Mont Royal 2:19:49 Verdun Neighbourhood Let's connect: ►Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/c/4KWanderings ►Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/4kWanderings ►Twitter: https://twitter.com/17NorthNE ►Instagram: https://instagram.com/17NNE ►TikTok: https://www.tiktok.com/@microwalks Intro music produced by Ryan Booth at The JamBooth Recording Studio. https://thejambooth.wixsite.com/music https://facebook.com/JamBoothMusic/ #4kwalk #walkingtour #streetlife #montreal #canada

title: 🇨🇦 Montreal Walking Tour | Pedestrian Street Design [4K Ultra HDR/60fps]
description: This week we're walking the Pedestrian Streets of Montréal. Pedestrian streets are particularly popular in Montréal, and are part of their unique urban landscape. Montréal's colourful streets encourage people to connect with places, and ensure the vibrancy of neighbourhoods and their businesses. The increased safety of pedestrian streets is also a big plus. With cars prohibited or tightly controlled, pedestrians feel much safer and the risk of accidents is much lower. Nuisances caused by vehicle traffic, such as stress and air and noise pollution, are also greatly reduced. Finally, the more spacious layout of these streets allows each walker to choose his or her own pace, regardless of physical condition, and encourages active mobility. The city is capitalizing on the great potential of local streets to create new neighbourhood public places where people can meet. Converting streets to pedestrian malls is part of this process and encourages appropriation of public spaces, discovery of local neighbourhoods and interactions between those who make them come alive. Montreal Mayor Valérie Plante has announced that 10 streets in the city will be pedestrian-only this summer. Montréal is a great city for walking and enjoying public places. The city will provide $12-million in funding for the pedestrianization of the commercial arteries spread over a three-year period. Pedestrian and shared-use streets, whether permanent or seasonal, provide a safe, enjoyable walking environment in the heart of the city. These colourful streets have become a signature and a staple of summer in Montreal. Try one out and you’ll discover new meeting places and opportunities for relaxation and entertainment in the heart of your favourite neighbourhoods. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Chapters: 0:00 Preview 4:00 Rue Saint-Catherine - The Village 58:00 Plateau - Mont Royal Avenue 2:19:48 Verdun - Wellington Street ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Intro music produced by Ryan Booth at The JamBooth Recording Studio. https://thejambooth.wixsite.com/music https://facebook.com/JamBoothMusic/ #montreal #travelcanada #4k #virtualtours #walkingtour

title: 🇫🇷 4K | The Complete Centre Pompidou Architecture Walking Tour [ 4K HDR / 60fps ]
description: Welcome to this stunning 4K HDR 60fps walking tour of the Centre Pompidou in Paris, designed by renowned architects Richard Rogers and Renzo Piano. This iconic building, inaugurated in 1977, is a true masterpiece of modern architecture and a must-see for anyone interested in art, design, and innovation. Join us as we explore all the levels of the Centre Pompidou, including the famous escalators and elevators, and the dynamic facade with its kinetic elements. One of the most distinctive features of the building's design is its exposed structural system, with brightly colored steel tubes, pipes, and ducts running along the exterior of the building. This design was a radical departure from traditional building designs, where such elements are typically hidden from view. We'll also take you through the unique architecture and design details that make this building so special and important in the history of modern architecture. The architects adopted an inside-out approach to the building's design, with the functional elements of the building, such as the elevators, escalators, and service areas, located on the exterior of the building, while the exhibition spaces and public areas were located on the interior. This approach not only maximized the usable space within the building but also created a unique and visually striking architectural design. The Centre Pompidou was designed to be a flexible and adaptable space, capable of accommodating a wide range of exhibitions and events. Its modular design, with movable partitions and flexible exhibition spaces, allows for easy reconfiguration to suit the needs of different exhibitions and events. The tour culminates in a visit to the upper lookout and garden, where you can enjoy breathtaking views of the city and reflect on the beauty of this architectural marvel. The use of bold colors, such as red, blue, and yellow, was intended to create a playful and vibrant atmosphere, in contrast to the more traditional, austere designs of many cultural institutions. Whether you're a fan of architecture, design, or simply enjoy exploring new places, this walking tour is not to be missed. So sit back, relax, and let us take you on a journey through the Centre Pompidou like never before. Don't forget to subscribe to our channel for more weekly walking tours of some of the most stunning buildings and landmarks in the world. Thanks for watching! #4kwalk #architecturetour #centrepompidou #richardrodgers
